explanation: Each fold doubles the thickness, and 42 doublings make over 4 trillion layers. At 0.1 mm each, that is about 440,000 km, more than the distance to the Moon.

claims.text: A sheet 0.1 mm thick folded in half 42 times would be about 440,000 km thick, more than the average Earth-Moon distance.
The stack would be far taller than a house, than Mount Everest and than the orbit of the International Space Station, about 400 km up.
Two multiplied by itself 42 times is about 4.4 trillion.
About 4.4 trillion layers of 0.1 mm make about 440,000 km.
The average distance from Earth to the Moon is about 384,400 km.
